sources.entry: The Battle for Wesnoth - The Battle for Wesnoth is an Open Source, turn-based tactical strategy game with a high fantasy theme, featuring both singleplayer and online/hotseat multiplayer combat. GPL-2.0 C++/deb
Battle for Wesnoth - Turn-based tactical strategy game, featuring both single-player and online multiplayer combat.

summary.one_liner: The Battle for Wesnoth is an open-source, turn-based tactical strategy game with a high fantasy theme, offering singleplayer campaigns plus online and hotseat multiplayer.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a turn-based tactical strategy game set in a high fantasy world, with campaigns that each have their own tactical challenges and multiple difficulty levels. It includes a map editor with many terrain types and the ability to save and share maps, scenarios, and campaigns. The game is highly moddable, supporting community map packs, eras, and campaigns. Online, local, and against-AI multiplayer are supported, along with configurable settings and hotkeys. Installation options named include Steam, itch.io, the macOS App Store, SourceForge installers, and Flatpak on Linux. Source builds are described in an INSTALL file.
use_cases: Multiplayer tactical battles against friends or AI
Installing a free strategy game on Windows, macOS, or Linux
Hotseat play with others on one computer
Contributing C++, Lua, or WML content to an open-source game
how_to_run: Install via Steam, itch.io, the macOS App Store, SourceForge installers, or Flatpak (Linux)
To build from source, see the INSTALL file in the repository
notable: Full open-source campaign game with a high fantasy setting and storyline
Built-in map editor with saving and sharing of maps and scenarios
Highly moddable through community maps, eras, and campaigns
Supports Windows, macOS, and Linux, with unofficial-style ports noted for iOS and Android
caveats: The iOS port is unmaintained and covers an older version (1.14)
The Android port is alpha and available only for version 1.19
Wesnoth lacks art for a variety of unit animations, per the README
summary.license: GPL-2.0 (source code under GNU GPL v2+; newer art contributions under CC BY-SA 4.0)
